newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK C.BANK SEES CROWN STEADY IF LIMIT REMOVED.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK C.BANK SEES CROWN STEADY IF LIMIT REMOVED.

text.p: The Slovak central bank on Tuesday said it did not expect a run on the crown if a plan to end citizens' annual limit on hard currency purchases is approved by parliament.

Scrapping the 60,000 crown annual limit on hard currency purchases by citizens is one of a series of amendments to a foreign exchange law, approved by the NBS governing board last Friday, aimed at further liberalisation of capital account operations according to OECD standards.

"There is no reason to expect that people will lose their confidence in crown and start massive purchases of hard currencies once the new law is valid," the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) spokesman, Jan Onda, told Reuters.
"Furthermore, according to our experience the current limit has been used only at up to 50 percent," Onda said. The NBS proposed the new legislation to become effective on June 1.

The second change to the law should cancel the so called "offer requirement for legal entities" and withdraw the present obligation according to which any legal subject had to ask for an NBS approval to open a foreign exchange account.
"The prepared law will effectively end this requirement and legal subjects should be allowed to hold hard currencies on their foreign exchange accounts without NBS approval," Onda said.
The NBS also drafted a change which should effectively allow Slovak branches of foreign banks to buy real estate in Slovakia.
The package of laws now must go to the parliament for final approval. "But the final date when the law will become valid will depend on the pace of further legislation procedures," Onda said.
